name: Auto Brightness+
description:
Auto Brightness+ puts a brightness slider for every monitor into Quick Settings, right next to the volume slider. External monitors are controlled over DDC/CI (ddcutil), laptop screens through the backlight.

* One thin slider per monitor; hover to see its name
* Automatic dimming per monitor: from sunset (or a set time) brightness goes down like the light outside and comes back in the morning; shape the evening on a small graph with the real sky behind it
* A simple menu: pick a value, one slider sets it (or a detailed menu with a slider for everything)
* Buttons that run by themselves at a time of the evening (e.g. turn the other screens off), undone in the morning
* Per monitor Night Light and red screen strength (×0–×2), extra dimming
* Lowest light with one click; turn a screen off, or all the other screens: clicks still reach the apps, the screen lights up smoothly while the mouse is on it
* Claude Code is done (optional): a notification, and the turned off screen with its terminal lights up
* Sunset from your location, the same way Night Light does it, without extra permissions
* Fast: monitor writes are merged and never block the desktop
* Available in 18 languages

External monitors need ddcutil and access to /dev/i2c-* (i2c group). Without it, sliders fall back to software dimming.

Made by Dukha.
